title: Prime Implicants, Essential Prime Implicants and the Minimal Cover
quickIdea: A prime implicant is a group that cannot be enlarged; an essential one covers a 1 that no other group covers; the minimal SOP is every essential prime implicant plus the cheapest way to cover what is left.
remember: An implicant is any product term that is 1 wherever the function is 1 - it never covers a 0. A prime implicant is an implicant that no larger implicant contains, so it is a maximal group on the map.
An essential prime implicant covers at least one 1 that no other prime implicant covers. That 1 is its witness, and every minimal SOP must contain the prime implicant.
The algorithm: circle every prime implicant, take all the essential ones, delete the 1s they cover, then choose the smallest set of the remaining prime implicants that covers the rest.

The cover is not always unique. When the leftover 1s can be covered in two equally cheap ways, two minimal SOPs exist with the same term and literal counts - and a multiple-select question can ask for both.
A don't care can never make a prime implicant essential. Only a real 1 can be a witness, which is why a group made entirely of don't cares is never forced into the answer.
Compare covers by literals, not by terms: three terms of two literals beat two terms of four literals when the cost is the number of gate inputs.

example.prompt: Find every prime implicant and every essential prime implicant of F(A,B,C) = Sigma m(0, 1, 2, 5, 6), and give all minimal SOPs.
example.work: On the 3-variable map the 1s are 000, 001, 010, 101, 110. Pairs: (0,1) gives A'B'; (0,2) gives A'C'; (1,5) gives B'C; (2,6) gives BC'. No pair can grow, so these four are the prime implicants. Minterm 5 is only in B'C and minterm 6 is only in BC', so both are essential. The leftover 1s are 0 and 2, and either A'B' or A'C' covers them - so two covers of equal cost exist.
example.answer: Prime implicants: A'B', A'C', B'C, BC'. Essential: B'C and BC'. The two minimal SOPs are A'B' + B'C + BC' and A'C' + B'C + BC', each three terms and six literals.

gateAngle: Two verified questions sit exactly here. GATE CSE 2018 Q.49 asks only for the number of essential prime implicants of a function with five don't cares (the answer is 3), and GATE CSE 2026 Set 1 Q.38 offers four four-term forms of which two are minimal - the two minimal covers of a function whose leftover 1s can be covered two ways.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2018 Q.49: F(P,Q,R,S) = Sigma m(0,2,5,7,9,11) + d(3,8,10,12,14). The number of essential prime implicants is ______.
variations.why: The prime implicants are Q'S', Q'R, PQ', PS', P'RS and P'QS. Minterm 0 is covered only by Q'S', minterm 5 only by P'QS and minterm 9 only by PQ', so those three are essential; the other three cover 1s that are already covered. The don't cares let Q'S' and PQ' grow to quads, but no don't care makes anything essential.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why can a group made only of don't cares never be an essential prime implicant?
variations.answer: Because an essential prime implicant needs a witness 1 that no other prime implicant covers, and a don't care is not a 1 that has to be covered at all.
variations.why: Leaving a don't care ungrouped costs nothing, so no cover is ever forced by one. This is the single most common mistake in counting essential prime implicants - GATE CSE 2018 Q.49 is built to punish it.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A four-variable function has prime implicants P1 = {0,1,8,9}, P2 = {0,2,8,10}, P3 = {5,7,13,15} and required 1s at 0, 1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 13, 15. How many minimal SOPs are there?
variations.answer: One: P3 is essential (minterm 5 and 15 appear nowhere else), and then P1 and P2 are both needed to cover 0, 1, 2, 8, 9 and 10, so the cover is P1 + P2 + P3.
variations.why: After taking the essential prime implicant, minterms 1 and 2 remain, and only P1 covers 1 while only P2 covers 2 - so both are forced. A cover is unique exactly when every leftover 1 is forced in this way.

trap.what: Counting a prime implicant as essential because it is the only group covering a don't care.
trap.why: Essentiality is defined on the 1s. A don't care is free to be 0, so a group whose only unique cell is a don't care is never forced.
trap.counterexample: In GATE CSE 2018 Q.49 the prime implicant PS' covers minterm 12 only as a don't care; taking PS' as essential would give 4 instead of the correct 3.

check.question: A 3-variable function has 1s at 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. List its prime implicants and say which are essential.
check.answer: Prime implicants: A' (cells 0,1,2,3) and B'C' (cells 0,4). A' is essential because minterms 1, 2 and 3 lie in no other prime implicant; B'C' is essential because minterm 4 lies in no other. So the minimal SOP is A' + B'C'.
check.explanation: The four cells of the first row form a quad and collapse to A'. Minterm 4 = 100 is alone in its row, and its only possible partner is m0, giving the pair B'C'. Both prime implicants have a witness, so both are essential and the cover is unique.
